note: Rows mirror the shape displacement_checks() emits ({prediction, verdict, observed, threshold, note}) with verdict PENDING, plus baseline_value / capable_of_varying / offline_replay_value as pending_primacy.json introduced. `elements` throughout means non-empty fields after splitting a final_kv value on comma, semicolon, newline or spaced slash -- i.e. meta_harness/candidates/chunk_limit/harness.py::count_elements, which a checker should import rather than re-derive. The parent is `baseline`, NOT `displacement`, so every no-change expectation is the baseline's value and not displacement's.
mechanism: MAX_KEYS bounds slots; nothing bounds information inside a slot. write_key admits at most MAX_KEYS enumerated elements per value (bound = MAX_KEYS itself, no new constant), never refuses the write, and names the loss in the tool result. Overflow policy, eviction order, recall() context construction, step(), prompts and tool descriptions are all the baseline's.

predictions.role: mechanism confirmation -- legs A (invariant) and B (behavioural), scored SEPARATELY
predictions.prediction: LEG A (invariant, guaranteed if injection worked): word_recognition mean elements/value <= 5.0, mean elements/store <= 16.0, max elements/value == 4. LEG B (the only behavioural measurement): mean distinct STUDIED words present in the store at most halves, <= 8.9, expected ~4.6
predictions.source: tasks/wm_word_recognition.jsonl final_kv; studied-word leg = distinct lowercase [a-z]+ tokens shared between the concatenated final_kv values and encoding_log.content
predictions.threshold: LEG A: elements_per_value_mean <= 5.0 AND elements_per_store_mean <= 16.0 AND elements_per_value_max == 4. LEG B: studied_words_in_store_mean <= 8.9 (half the baseline's 17.78). THIRD OUTCOME, neither pass nor fail: studied_words in 8.9-16 WITH leg A satisfied means the bound held and the agent REALLOCATED to fill the 16-element ceiling -- record as adaptation, not as a mechanism failure.
predictions.capable_of_varying: yes -- 13.21 elements/value observed in the iteration-0 baseline run and 16.29 in the iteration-1 displacement run, max 99 and 93 respectively; replaying all 49 real write sequences through the real ChunkBoundedMemory class bounds 113 values and drops 2309 elements, with replay fidelity 1.000 against the observed final_kv
predictions.note: This is the analogue of displacement's n=3 `answered` 6.82 -> 14.00. LEG A is an invariant of the rule, in the same class as P3 -- if elements_per_store_mean stays above 16 the bound is not being applied at all and the run is void. LEG B is the only part that measures behaviour, and it is a bet on the agent's strategy, not a consequence of the rule: the bound permits 4 slots x 4 elements = 16 elements, so a run in which the agent reallocates -- four slots each holding four studied words instead of one slot holding 99 -- would sit at ~16 against a baseline of 17.78, i.e. the rule alone guarantees only a ~10% reduction on this leg. The replay's 4.62 arises because the observed sequences dump the list into a single `recent_items` slot, leaving the other three holding non-list content. The studied-word count is proof against PUNCTUATION gaming (a space-separated list satisfies an element count trivially while keeping every word); it is NOT proof against slot reallocation, which is the separate channel the third outcome records.

Two-sided on purpose -- truncation keeps the opening of a value and drops trailing clauses, so if the dropped clauses were the paraphrased ones precision could RISE.
